critical_code_review_comments: server.py:13096-13121 — Guard now correctly relies on relation predicates (is_admin | is_coordinatore | is_linked_parent | is_self_athlete | is_authorized_staff). Reads cleanly and short-circuits before verified-flag handling. Consider extracting a shared helper `user_can_edit_athlete_certificate(user, athlete)` because the same 5-branch check is likely to be re-used in the upcoming PDF-upload and delete endpoints.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_certificate_relation_auth.py is idempotent and self-restoring; safe to re-run. Case (m) multi-tenant regression is currently skipped: to enable, seed a user with known credentials belonging to a society_id different from 697fdba0d218717959e73eea and adapt the last test (login + POST -> 403).
rca_of_issue: Original bug (403 'Non hai i permessi per aggiornare certificati' for a genuinely linked parent whose role != 'parent'): POST /certificates/simple used a role whitelist before checking parent_id/second_parent_id, so a user linked as parent but stored with role=coach/coordinator/viewer was rejected. Fix at server.py:13096-13121 now derives authorization from the RELATION (is_linked_parent OR is_self_athlete OR is_authorized_staff OR is_admin OR is_coordinatore). Verified: (a) parent+linked -> 200, (b) coach-role linked as parent_id -> 200 (was 403 before fix), (c) parent-role but unrelated -> 403, (d) admin same society -> 200, (e) viewer assigned to team -> 200, round-trip GET + athlete document sync work. Multi-tenant isolation cannot be end-to-end tested with current DB (single society); code path relies on relation predicates which all fail for a foreign-society, unrelated user, so 403 is expected by inspection.
